annotations.title: Set what agents may do with files

description: The RULES BOARD for files, folders and web sites on this computer: what an AI agent may do with each one — allowed, ask the user, clean copy only, or not allowed — optionally only for certain agents (claude-code, cursor …) or sub-agents, at certain times, or for certain actions (read, search, run, write; on a site: browse, interact) or file types. A web site rule (site:'example.com', its subdomains too; site:'*' = every site) holds an agent that drives a browser over MCP or fetches a page: browse = open or read a page, interact = click, type, submit. e.g. {action:'add', site:'bank.example.com', effect:'ask', actions:'interact'} = the user approves every click there (the human checkpoint: a CAPTCHA, a login, a payment is the user's to pass, never the agent's). An allowed site is also a TRUSTED DESTINATION: after the session read a web page, an API answer or a partner's command, a network step waits for a person, except a curl / wget whose every address is a named allowed site (https, no proxy, no -k; site:'*' does not count). e.g. {action:'add', site:'api.elevenlabs.io', effect:'allow', actions:'run'} trusts only commands to it. A TRUSTED MCP SERVER is the same for another server's tools: after outside content, a tool that writes through another MCP server waits for a person, except the tools the owner named: {action:'add', server:'dreamz', tools:['render_take','take_status'], effect:'allow'} (server as in mcp__<server>__<tool>; each tool named exactly, no wildcard, never the whole server; a tool that sends a message to people, send, reply, forward, email, message, post, comment, invite, share, publish, is never trusted; agent, hours, days and origin may scope it). Several rules per file or folder; the most specific path decides, and among its rules the first whose conditions hold. Enforced by NoData's read gate on every read, search, command and write, and on every page an agent opens or acts on through a browser tool or WebFetch, whatever the agent. Plain fields, no condition syntax needed: folder (or path), effect, agent ("cursor", ["cursor","windsurf"] or "all but cursor"), sub_agent ("main" = the main conversation, "all but main" = only sub-agents), actions ("write", ["read","search"] or "all but read"), hours ([18,8] or "18-8", this computer's clock, wraps overnight), days ([0,1,2,3,4] or "sun-thu"). e.g. {action:'add', folder:'~/Finance', effect:'deny', agent:'cursor', actions:'write', hours:'18-8'} = cursor may not write in Finance at night. action 'list' shows every rule. 'add' adds one (tightening asks for confirm:true; ALLOW needs the user's own approval). 'remove' removes rule n (removing a restriction needs the user's approval). action 'level' with level:'strict'|'routine'|'production' = APPROVAL LEVELS, how often an agent stops for the user: strict = every stop; routine = also lets an install of what the project already pins pass after outside content, and lets nodata_run run a command to trusted sites without a dialog when its keys allow an agent; production = also an answer from a trusted site does not mark the session (closed on an organisation's computers until an admin opens it). Writes to what runs the gate, NoData's keys, credentials in the chat and an agent approving itself stop at every level. Raising a level needs the user's approval; lowering it does not. Every step a level lets through is counted. A rule may name a kind of step: {action:'add', step:'install', effect:'deny'} = no installs at all; {action:'add', step:'push', effect:'ask'} = every git push asks. action 'set' with set:'developer' adds a ready-made set in one step: this computer's credential folders (SSH, GitHub, npm, cloud logins) never read by an agent, writes to .github and migrations asked first (with what the change does), clicks on github.com and npmjs.com asked first. It previews; confirm:true adds every rule not already on the board. Advanced conditions (added to the plain fields): [{field, op, value}] with fields action, time.hour, time.weekday, file.ext, file.name, agent, agent.type, org, origin; e.g. [{"field":"time.hour","op":"between","value":[18,8]}] = at night; [{"field":"action","op":"eq","value":"write"}] = writes only; [{"field":"agent","op":"eq","value":"claude-code"}] = only that agent; [{"field":"agent.type","op":"ne","value":"main"}] = only sub-agents (main = the main conversation). An agent the gate cannot name meets every restricting rule scoped to agents, and no allowing one. action 'approve' with checkpoint:"<id>" = the human checkpoint: when the gate holds a step on a site whose rule asks, it gives an id; this asks the computer's owner to approve that one step in the browser and waits; then repeat the same call. The agent cannot approve it.

actions.description: add: which actions — on files: read, search, run, write; on a site: browse, interact. "write", ["read","search"], or "all but read". Omit = every action.

agent.description: add: which agent the rule is for: "cursor", ["cursor","windsurf"], or "all but claude-code". Omit = every agent.

approval.description: The code the user approved (loosening only).

checkpoint.description: approve: the id the gate gave for a held step on a web site.

confirm.description: add/remove a restriction: true = do it. Omit to preview.

days.description: add: only on these weekdays: [5,6], ["fri","sat"] or "sun-thu" (0 = Sunday).

effect.description: add: what happens when an agent touches it.

folder.description: add: same as path — the folder (or file) the rule is for. ~/Name = in the home folder; **/Name = any folder with that name.

hours.description: add: only at these hours on this computer's clock: [18,8] or "18-8" (wraps overnight).

level.description: level: the approval level to take — strict, routine or production. Omit to see the current one and what each does.

note.description: add: a few words the user will see when the rule decides.

path.description: add: the file or folder (a folder covers everything inside it).

server.description: add: one MCP server whose named tools are trusted past the hold after outside content (allow only): its name as in mcp__<server>__<tool>, e.g. "dreamz" or "plugin:dreamz:dreamz". Needs tools.

set.description: set: the ready-made rule set to add ('developer').

site.description: add: a web site instead of a folder: "example.com" (its subdomains too), "https://shop.example.com", or "*" for every site. Effects: allow, ask, deny.

step.description: add: a kind of outbound step instead of a folder or site: install, install_locked, push, publish, send, launch_agent, instructions, click, fetch, mcp_send. Effects: allow (answers only the hold after outside content), ask, deny.

sub_agent.description: add: which sub-agent inside the agent: "main" = the main conversation, "all but main" = only sub-agents.

tools.description: add, with server: the exact tools to trust, ["render_take","take_status"]. No wildcard; a messaging tool (send, reply, email, post, share …) is refused.
